hero.lede: I'm Naod, a full-stack developer. For 5+ years I've built SaaS products, e-commerce platforms and APIs for 17+ clients, covering the database, the business logic, the integrations between systems and the interface on top.

about.statement: I build the whole product: the schema, the services, the integrations and the interface people use.
bio: My work spans the full stack: Laravel and PHP services, MySQL schemas and queries, REST APIs and the integrations between systems, and React, Livewire and Alpine.js interfaces on top. At Barecare that means a multi-service commerce platform: a storefront, a warehouse system, a B2B shop and an influencer platform that all have to agree with one another.

The work I'm best at happens where systems meet: an order that has to exist in two databases, a checkout that must never submit twice, a listing that quietly runs a query for every row. Those problems cost real money, and they only show up when you understand every layer involved.

I started out building interfaces, and it still shows in how I work: APIs designed around the screens that consume them, queries shaped around what a page actually needs, and performance treated as part of the product rather than an afterthought.

impact.intro: The problems I solve best sit between layers and between systems: where a page meets the database, and where one service has to agree with another.

highlights.label: Database queries per page on a warehouse admin listing
highlights.context: Barecare’s warehouse purchase-order listing loaded each row’s vendor, documents and quantities separately. Eager loading and SQL aggregates brought it to a constant three queries.

highlights.label: Page load time on the same listing
highlights.context: The direct result of cutting those queries: the listing went from about four seconds to under one.
